title: L2 stability of square roots of bounded positive three-dimensional Coulomb or gravitational Vlasov-Poisson solutions with mixed derivative control
source_title: On the $L^2$ rate of convergence in the limit from the Hartree to the Vlasov–Poisson equation
author: Jacky J. Chong; Laurent Lafleche; Chiara Saffirio
difficulty_reason: Passing to square roots does not by itself close an L2 stability estimate for the Coulomb field. The author decomposes the singular interaction into two terms and bounds one by endpoint Lorentz control, while the other requires Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev, velocity Cauchy-Schwarz and a different spatial mixed-norm estimate. Those two source-specific closures produce the exact integrated coefficient before the routine Gronwall step, rather than treating Gronwall or the advanced equation name as the difficulty.

Exponent explicitly uses rho_f2 Lx_infty and gradient_xi sqrt(f2) in Lx3Lxi2 and Lx3,1Lxi1; finite time-integrated coefficient gives meaningful stability. historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The proof uses the square-root transport equation to split the nonlinear Coulomb field difference into quadratic and mixed terms, combining an endpoint Lorentz bound with mixed-norm Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev control. This weak-strong kinetic stability estimate goes beyond qualifying-exam PDE tools in its nonlinear singular-field application.
